### Formula 1 — Monster HP Scaling

```
scaled_hp = base_hp × wave_hp_multiplier × difficulty_hp_multiplier

wave_hp_multiplier       = 1 + (hp_wave_growth_rate × (wave_index - 1))
difficulty_hp_multiplier = 1 + (hp_difficulty_growth_rate × (difficulty_tier - 1))
```

|----------|------|-------|-------------|
| `base_hp` | float | 40–800 | HP at wave 1, Normal difficulty. Authored per MonsterResource. |
| `wave_index` | int | 1–8 | Current wave number within the mission. |
| `difficulty_tier` | int | 1–3 | Player-selected difficulty: 1=Normal, 2=Hard, 3=Brutal. |
| `hp_wave_growth_rate` | float | 0.12–0.20 | Per-wave fractional HP increase. Tuning knob. Default: 0.15 |
| `hp_difficulty_growth_rate` | float | 0.25–0.50 | Per-difficulty-tier fractional HP increase. Tuning knob. Default: 0.35 |
| `wave_hp_multiplier` | float | 1.00–2.40 | HP scale factor from wave progression. |
| `difficulty_hp_multiplier` | float | 1.00–2.00 | HP scale factor from difficulty selection. |
| `scaled_hp` | float | 40–3840 | Immutable HP assigned at spawn. Floored at 1.0. |

design_evidence.section: Mission Select System > Acceptance Criteria > Group 2 — Difficulty Tier Selection & Completion Tracking (Rules 3, 4; Formula 3)
design_evidence.text:
### Group 2 — Difficulty Tier Selection & Completion Tracking (Rules 3, 4; Formula 3)

- **AC-4**: GIVEN a mission with `recommended_difficulty_tier = 2`, WHEN the player enters CONFIGURING for that mission, THEN `difficulty_tier` defaults to `2` without any player input, and the player may change it to `1` or `3` before Launch with no validation blocking any of the three values.
- **AC-5** *(the silent-tier-change assumption — dedicated AC)*: GIVEN the player is in CONFIGURING and changes the difficulty tier selection three times in a row (e.g., 2 → 1 → 3), WHEN every EventBus emission during this sequence is recorded, THEN zero events fire as a result of the tier changes themselves — no `difficulty_tier_selected` or equivalent event exists or is emitted. The only observable signal of the final tier choice is the `difficulty_tier` field inside `mission_launched`, fired once, at confirm time. This explicitly tests the silence Rule 3 asserts, not merely assumes it.

design_evidence.section: Mission Select System > Detailed Design > Core Rules
design_evidence.text:
- **Registry action**: `cell_size` (value `64.0`, unit: world units per grid cell) should be added to `design/registry/entities.yaml` as a project-wide constant, sourced from this GDD, referenced by `design/gdd/grid-system.md`. Flagged at the end of this session per the standard cross-system-fact protocol.

3. **Difficulty tier selection.** The player picks exactly one `difficulty_tier: int` (1=Normal, 2=Hard, 3=Brutal) per mission attempt, matching `monster.md`'s registered enum and range exactly — this GDD does not redefine or rename the tier set. Default selection on entering CONFIGURING (Rule 6) is `recommended_difficulty_tier` from the `MissionEntry`, but the player may freely change it to any of the 3 values before launch. There is no dedicated EventBus event for a tier *change* — no `difficulty_tier_selected` event exists in the frozen event contract (`event-bus.md`), and this GDD does not invent one (assumption flagged below). The selected value is communicated exactly once, at confirm time, as the `difficulty_tier` field of `mission_launched`.

implementation_evidence.text:
class_name DifficultyRewards
extends RefCounted
## Reward multiplier per difficulty tier (1 Normal, 2 Hard, 3 Brutal, 4+ Ascension).
##
## Decided 2026-10-15 (production/balance/progression-targets.md): harder runs
## must pay noticeably more than Normal so they are the fastest route through
## the campaign. Applied to hero XP (Hero.set_reward_multiplier) and material
## drops + mission-end surplus (ResourceEconomy.set_tier_reward_multiplier).
## In-mission gold is not scaled: it resets every mission and is balanced
## against tower costs, not progression.
##
## Ascension (2026-11-03, endgame): tiers above Brutal. Clearing a map's
## highest tier opens the next one on that map (MissionSelect), up to
## MAX_ASCENSION ranks. Each rank multiplies monster HP by ASCENSION_HP_GROWTH
## and rewards by ASCENSION_REWARD_GROWTH on top of Brutal, so late-game hero
## power keeps meeting resistance (tower-defense pitfall: enemy HP must keep
## pace with player power). Rewards grow slower than HP on purpose: each rank
## is a real step up, and the best farm is the highest rank you can clear
## reliably, not the highest one at all.

const TIER_MULTIPLIERS: Array[float] = [1.0, 1.3, 1.7]

design_evidence.section: Monster System > Edge Cases > Category 7: Formula Boundary Edge Cases
design_evidence.text:
**EC-7.3 — `tarot_speed_scalar` is 0**
Situation: Tarot modifier fires `mission_modifier_applied` with `modifier_value = 0.0`.
What happens: Formula 2 computes `scaled_speed = base_speed × multiplier × 0.0 = 0.0`. Monster System floors `scaled_speed` at 0.1 cells/sec. All monsters spawned after this modifier are near-stationary. Monsters already ACTIVE retain their previously assigned `scaled_speed` (modifier applies at instantiation only, not retroactively). The Tarot GDD must bound `monster_speed_scalar` modifier values at minimum 0.50 — the floor is a safety net, not a design target.

implementation_evidence.text:
class_name ActiveSlowEffect
extends RefCounted

## One in-flight slow instance on a MonsterEntity. design/gdd/damage-status.md
## Formula D6 (amended 2026-08-13 — slow moves into scope alongside burn/poison,
## see Rule I.3). Unlike ActiveStatusEffect (burn/poison), this has no ticks —
## it is a continuous speed multiplier that decays by wall-clock duration and
## is read fresh every frame by Monster System's movement pass, never applied
## by mutating MonsterEntity.scaled_speed (which stays immutable after spawn
## per ADR-0006's own Key Interfaces contract).
##
## Multiple instances stack multiplicatively (a design decision, not an
## oversight — see the GDD): two 15% slows combine to 0.85 x 0.85 = 72.25% of
## original speed, not a summed 30% reduction. This structurally guarantees
## effective speed can never reach zero or go negative regardless of how many
## instances are active, with no separate clamp needed at the combination site.

var remaining_duration: float = 0.0
## 1.0 - effect_value, clamped to [SPEED_MULTIPLIER_FLOOR, 1.0] — see
## MonsterManager.SPEED_MULTIPLIER_FLOOR's own doc comment for the floor's purpose.
var speed_multiplier: float = 1.0

## Product of every active slow instance's speed_multiplier (1.0 if none are
## active) — the multiplicative-stacking combination rule from Formula D6.
## Never mutates entity.scaled_speed itself.
func _effective_speed(entity: MonsterEntity) -> float:
	if entity.stun_remaining > 0.0:
		return 0.0
	var multiplier: float = 1.0
	for slow: ActiveSlowEffect in entity.active_slow_effects:
		multiplier *= slow.speed_multiplier
	return entity.scaled_speed * multiplier


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pass 1b — Status Effects (burn/poison DoT ticks + slow duration decay)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## damage-status.md Formula D6. speed_multiplier is 1.0 - effect_value, floored
## at SPEED_MULTIPLIER_FLOOR — never applied by mutating scaled_speed (immutable
## after spawn per ADR-0006).
func _apply_slow_effect(target_monster_id: int, effect_value: float, effect_duration: float) -> void:
	var entity: MonsterEntity = _entity_lookup.get(target_monster_id) as MonsterEntity
	if entity == null or entity.lifecycle_state == MonsterEntity.State.DEAD:
		return
	var slow := ActiveSlowEffect.new()
	slow.remaining_duration = effect_duration
	slow.speed_multiplier = maxf(SPEED_MULTIPLIER_FLOOR, 1.0 - effect_value)
	entity.active_slow_effects.append(slow)

design_evidence.section: Tower System > Formulas > Formula 3: Tower HP
design_evidence.text:
**Output Range:** 80–1000. Floor (80): Tier 1 Foundation with minimum base HP. Ceiling (1000): Tier 4 fully upgraded.

**Boss damage calibration** *(Provisional — validate against Monster System GDD boss damage formula before implementation. Do not treat these numbers as authoritative until cross-referenced.)*: The Monster GDD specifies two boss tiers: early-wave bosses (base_damage 15–25, wave-scaled) and final-wave bosses (base_damage **55–80**, wave-scaled — **corrected 2026-07-15, `/review-all-gdds`**: was still 40–80 here after Monster GDD's own `/design-review` narrowed the final-wave floor from 40 to 55 on 2026-07-15 to fix a boundary failure at wave 5). At Wave 8 max scale (×1.7): final boss deals ~136 HP/hit at maximum. At the earliest legal final-wave point (wave 5, base_damage=55, ×1.40): ~77 HP/hit. Against a Tier 1 minimum-HP tower (80 HP): expect 1 hit destruction at the high end. **A Tier 1 minimum-HP tower should expect 1–2 hits from a final-wave boss; a Tier 2 tower (min 120 HP) should expect 1 hit. design_evidence.text:
### Formula 3 — BOSS Attack Damage

**Two BOSS calibration tiers** — early-wave and final-wave BOSSes use different `base_damage` values. The registered `tower_hp_boss_damage_provisional_range` [40–200 HP/hit] applies to **final-wave BOSSes** only.


**Boundary-value correction (2026-07-15, `/design-review`):** the prior table checked only wave=8/base_damage=50, which obscured a real boundary failure — at the earliest legal final-wave point (wave=5, `base_damage`=the prior floor of 40), `boss_effective_damage = 40 × 1.40 = 56`, giving `ceil(1000/56) = 18` hits against a Tier 4 tower, above the documented 8–15 hit target. Rather than loosen the target (which would let a final-wave boss feel passive/inert on its earliest legal wave — a Player Fantasy concern, not just a math one), the final-wave `base_damage` floor was raised 40→55, which brings the worst case to 13 hits, inside target. **The Tier 1 "3–5 hits" target in Rule 18 was never actually achievable against a final-wave boss at any authored value** (a final-wave boss's minimum damage, even at the old 40 floor, always kills a Tier 1 tower in 1–2 hits) — that target only ever applied to early-wave bosses; Rule 18's prose is corrected below to state this scoping explicitly rather than leaving it as an unstated assumption.

design_evidence.section: Monster System > Acceptance Criteria > Area 7: Formula Correctness
design_evidence.text:
GIVEN a BOSS MonsterResource authored at the final-wave `base_damage` floor of **55** (narrowed 2026-07-15 from the prior floor of 40), spawned at `wave_index=5` (earliest legal final-wave index), `boss_dmg_wave_growth_rate=0.10`,
WHEN `boss_effective_damage` is calculated via Formula 3,
THEN `boss_effective_damage == 77.0` (`55 × 1.40`); hits-to-kill vs. a Tier 4 tower (1000 HP) is `ceil(1000/77) == 13`, inside the documented 8–15 hit target. **AND GIVEN** the same BOSS is authored at the old, now-invalid floor of `base_damage=40`, **THEN** load-time validation must reject this as an authoring error — `base_damage` below 55 is no longer valid for a final-wave (`wave_index ∈ [5,8]`) BOSS MonsterResource.

**AC-45** `[Logic · BLOCKING]` *(added 2026-07-15, `/design-review` — closes a regression gap: AC-26 only exercises the 5-wave-mission case where wave 4 is coincidentally both the fixed worked-example index and the true penultimate wave, so a future regression toward hardcoded "wave 4 is special" logic would not be caught)*
